active.body:
The most recent Rubin data `tocsin` has reached is MJD 61305.42, which is 41.6 days behind now. The broker mirror normally lags ~16 days; the limit here is 30.

The channel itself is fine — it is running on schedule and committing results. What has stopped is the DATA. A screen re-reading the same frontier every night produces a clean null indefinitely and looks healthy from every other angle, which is why this check exists separately from the staleness check.

Check whether ALeRCE is still ingesting the LSST alert stream before reading any recent null from this channel.

**Cause established 2026-11-02 by `rubin-outage`: SKY_STOPPED.** Independent brokers stop on the same night (ALeRCE 2026-10-31; fink 2026-10-31), so the alert stream itself stopped and no change to the broker path recovers data that was never taken. Do not relax the threshold on this — the condition is real. See `docs/rubin-outage.md`. ZTF, the other public wide-field alert stream, is LIVE (newest night 2026-11-02 via alerce_ztf), so `tocsin-altfeeds` has a current feed to lean on.
active.title: TOCSIN is screening data 42 days old

active.body:
`loom` has advanced from MJD 61235.41627 to MJD 61344.31881 — 108.9 days of sky — after sitting still since 2026-07-30T13:13:46Z.

The stall was confirmed across 95.4 days of sightings; the advance itself happened between 2026-11-02T22:47:07Z and now, so the interval between successive frontier values is 95.4 days. That is an UPPER BOUND on the mirror's true ingest gap — this repository samples the frontier about once a day and cannot see a change finer than that.

The frontier is now 2.7 days behind the wall clock, inside the 30-day limit, so the age alert clears. That is not the same as current: the mirror's ordinary lag is ~16 days, and anything above that is still backlog.

This is the cadence datum `FRONTIER_STALL_DAYS` has never had — it was set to 7 by guesswork because no advance had ever been observed here. Recalibrate it against `observed_advance_days` in `results/alerts/frontier.json` now that there is one.

Note that the nights lost to the stall are ABSENT, not null: they were never observed, so they add nothing to the screen's trial count and must not be counted as clean sky.
active.title: LOOM's data frontier is moving again (+108.9 days of sky)

active.body:
The `asassn` adapter reached its service but has no usable path to a light curve.

Reason recorded by the probe: no cone request was accepted (every variant and format in the matrix above), and the vendor client cannot be imported here -- so there is no path to a light curve, only to metadata

A screen over this feed would run, commit and report nothing found -- which is indistinguishable from a quiet sky and is not a result. Read `results/tocsin_altfeeds/probe.json`; the request matrix there records responses and connection errors.
active.title: ASASSN cannot serve light curves
